items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: I saw them out there, even Ella — she was out there working for George Wein doing one- nighters in Europe.

ctx.x: Okay. Did you get a sense, eventually, that playing music for a living can be challenging, from a perhaps paying your rent aspect? Supporting a family?

Yeah. I never really thought about it and I never struggled. I mean you know it wasn’t like I was in affluence all the time either. But I never struggled to pay the rent and to live and to raise a family. The phone rang and it would escalate. In other words I’d get a call from Bob Wilber, next thing you know I’m touring for six years with him in Europe, next thing you know I meet Suzanne Somers and she says I want you as my band leader, and that’s a whole story in itself. I left the jazz world as we know it, to…

I noticed the same thing when I started doing these interviews and it shocked me at first and then it didn’t shock me anymore, and that is when a person that I was interviewing who was like a hero of mine, someone that I’d followed for decades, and at the end of the interview they would, well, hit me up for a gig.
